title: Two Giant Black Holes May Be Heading for a Crash
summary:
Most big galaxies have a huge black hole in the middle. These supermassive black holes can weigh millions or even billions of times as much as the Sun. Scientists want to know how they grow so big. One idea is that two black holes can join together.

A team led by Silke Britzen in Germany studied a galaxy called Mrk 501. Its black hole shoots out a jet of tiny particles at nearly the speed of light. The team looked at radio data from about 23 years. They found a second jet moving in a different direction. That is a strong clue that a second black hole is there.

"It came as a complete surprise," Britzen said.

The team thinks the two black holes circle each other about every 121 days. They might crash together and merge in as little as 100 years. That is very fast for space!
why_it_matters: It helps us understand the giant objects at the centers of galaxies, including our own.
